Before March 2026 the internal escalation contact for a suspected gas leak was the Facilities Lead.

From March 2026 that internal escalation contact was replaced by the 24-hour Estates Helpdesk.

Before January 2026, the policy required a resident assessed at high risk to be repositioned at least every 4 hours.

After the change (the version authoritative at and after 2026‑01‑01), the interval for a resident assessed at high risk was tightened to repositioning at least every 2 hours.

On identifying two people at the same site with the same suspected infection onset within 48 hours, declare an outbreak immediately: the registered manager declares the outbreak and notifies the local Health Protection Team the same day, begin enhanced cleaning in affected areas using the product/frequency advised by the Health Protection Team or the site infection lead, cohort affected people (and where practicable staff) away from unaffected people, restrict or reshape communal activities per the Visiting Arrangements Policy exception, and monitor and log staff and residents' symptoms daily for the duration of the outbreak.

Record-keeping: retain a daily case log tracking new cases against the incubation period and a brief dated decision log of every significant outbreak decision (for example when enhanced cleaning began, when cohorting was applied or relaxed), since the registered manager must keep these records to show the process was followed and to support later review or regulatory enquiry.
The mileage claim will be paid with your next salary run.

The current (April 2026) version increased both payments: the one-off starter (initial) uniform allowance was raised to £55, and the annual April replacement allowance was raised to £35.

Under the prior version these amounts were lower: the one-off starter initial allowance had been £40, and the annual April replacement allowance had been £25.

Recorded policy scope

The recorded scope of "Key Safe Procedure" includes "Oakfield Lodge". This is a statement of recorded policy applicability only; it does not establish what action is safe or required. The reason for this scope is not established by the scope record.

Other requested guidance

The Midlands key-safe procedure explicitly extends to cover Oakfield Lodge’s outreach service as the region-wide policy replacing the Willow-Bank-only version.

The procedure requires that any client key safe code change be reported to the office within 24 hours.

The rule did not change: both the earlier and the current policy state that a limited list of over-the-counter/homely remedies (paracetamol, antacid, simple cough syrup) may be given without a prescription, recorded on the MAR/chart and subject to the person’s care plan not excluding it.

Where a genuinely novel hazard arises that no existing risk assessment covers, the registered manager must arrange an immediate interim control measure and escalate the matter for a formal risk assessment; if the hazard cannot be fully resolved immediately the area should be cordoned off and appropriate warnings placed while fuller resolution is arranged.

Risk assessments, incident records, training records and each year’s annual health and safety report must be retained in accordance with the Records Retention Schedule.

For a sector-wide emergency affecting every site, teams should take consistent guidance from the Health and Safety Lead's organisation-level emergency coordination group, which becomes the single point of truth and issues consistent guidance to every site.

The organisation-wide debrief after a sector-wide emergency is run by the Health and Safety Lead's coordination group, which holds an organisation-wide debrief covering every affected site.

The updated version leads with family communication first—family contact and invitation for feedback are presented before the brief Quality Committee death review; the previous version presented the brief review and Quality Committee step earlier, with family contact described afterward.

No, the underlying requirements did not change—the update reordered the sections to describe family communication first but explicitly states that no actual requirement was changed.
If you are an existing HQ (Central Support Office) DSE user, repeat the DSE self‑assessment annually or after a workstation change; new starters complete it during their first week.

Overtime worked on a bank holiday is paid at 1.5 times the standard hourly rate under the current guidance.

The older guidance likewise specified a 1.5 times rate for overtime worked on a bank holiday, so the same 1.5x bank holiday rate applied in the previous version as well.

If an external agency does not acknowledge your referral, the registered manager should follow the escalation steps: contact the agency’s own duty line to follow up, and if the agency still has not resolved or acknowledged the referral within a further 2 working days, inform the organisation‑level Safeguarding Lead, who may escalate directly within that agency or use the local Safeguarding Adults Board’s escalation route (the post‑referral checklist also instructs following up directly with the agency within 2 working days if acknowledgment is not confirmed). A separate requirement is to complete a post‑referral review within 10 working days of any external referral. 

You must keep a record of the external referral and its post‑referral review outcome in the confidential safeguarding file: every external referral (including to the Office of the Public Guardian or Action Fraud) and its post‑referral review outcome is retained in the confidential safeguarding file in line with the Records Retention Schedule, and safeguarding records are retained for 8 years after the person’s last contact with Alderbridge; these records are stored separately from the general care file with more restricted access.
